causal.assumptions_right: AUDCAD was the right isolation of an Australia-versus-Canada residual. A dollar pair would have mixed Fed and common-commodity beta into a view that was supposed to be AU versus CA.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The fade needed housing and BoC path time measured in weeks, but the book was managed as a two-to-three-day overnight trade. Higher Australian carry versus Canada, and any afternoon oil-diplomacy tape, were treated as exit reasons rather than noise around a longer horizon.
causal.causal_divergence: The loss was a horizon mismatch, not a failed cross isolation. A slow valuation residual was forced through a short holding period and abandoned at an unchanged mid instead of waiting for the housing or BoC invalidation that had justified the short.
causal.future_implication: Do not fade a multi-year non-USD extreme on a two-to-three-day clock, and do not reverse the same cross when the original housing or BoC invalidation has not printed.
causal.observed_reality: The short opened 19 Sep near 1.00 and was closed 22 Sep near 1.00 after about two and a half days, realizing about -49945, then immediately flipped long in the same pair. The richness residual did not compress on that overnight clock.
causal.original_belief: The 19 Sep short treated AUDCAD near 1.00 as a multi-year richness extreme that isolated an Australian housing slowdown against a still-open Canadian hike path, so fading the cross was cleaner than shorting AUDUSD or buying USDCAD.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same 19 Sep richness and housing-versus-hike facts, an explicit multi-week horizon would have kept the short through 22 Sep or stayed out of an expression the overnight clock could not host. It would not have closed unchanged at 1.00 and reversed.

items.expression_assessment: AUDCAD remained cleaner than USD pairs. Expression was not the failure; horizon and the subsequent reverse were.
items.future_rule: If an AUDCAD fade needs housing or BoC path time longer than the overnight holding clock, stay flat rather than fade and then flip the same cross.
items.lesson: A multi-year AUDCAD richness fade is a multi-week relative-value book, not a two-to-three-day overnight fade, and closing it unchanged does not authorize a reverse.
items.thesis_assessment: The AU-CA residual in AUDCAD was coherent. The error was forcing that residual onto an overnight horizon that could not deliver the housing and BoC path the thesis needed.
items.timing_assessment: Holding period was about two and a half days against a thesis that needed housing and BoC path time. That is a horizon error, not a tick-entry miss.
items.what_failed: The short was exited as if a multi-year percentile extreme would compress inside one overnight cycle, then replaced by the opposite side of the same pair.
items.what_worked: Keeping the residual in AUDCAD rather than a USD pair was the correct expression of an Australia-versus-Canada view.

causal.assumptions_right: AUDCAD still isolated AU versus CA without a dollar common factor, and oil remains the Canadian terms-of-trade swing that can break an AUDCAD long.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Afternoon diplomacy was treated as a regime change in CAD energy premium. The stated invalidation already included an oil hold or spike that re-supports CAD. That oil risk was underweighted relative to owning the new tape after cutting the short.
causal.causal_divergence: The long was not a new Australia-versus-Canada differential. It was a catalyst reverse of an unfinished richness fade. When oil stayed high enough to support CAD, the diplomacy skim did not dominate and the pair drifted from 1.00 toward 0.99.
causal.future_implication: Flattening a horizon-mismatched fade is not a signal to own the opposite side of the same non-USD residual. Require a new policy, growth, inflation, or carry gap before re-entering AUDCAD.
causal.observed_reality: The long opened 22 Sep near 1.00 and closed 29 Sep near 0.99, realizing about -35788. The diplomacy-driven CAD discount did not arrive. The pair leaked lower and was flattened as the wrong side of the same residual. Frozen AUDCAD is 0.99321 with Brent 102.59.
causal.original_belief: On 22 Sep the seat treated afternoon Hormuz diplomacy and a Saudi restart as enough to skim CAD energy premium while an Australian hike stayed priced, so flipping the closed short into a smaller AUDCAD long would isolate that new AU-over-CA catalyst better than AUDUSD.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: If the 22 Sep close of the short had been followed by a flat book instead of a reverse, the same oil and diplomacy information would have been observed from zero risk, and the long P&L path would not have existed.

items.expression_assessment: AUDCAD was still cleaner than USD pairs. The error was direction and catalyst, not choosing a dollar pair.

facts.invalidation: Oil hold/spike that re-supports CAD terms-of-trade, Hormuz diplomacy failure, or AU dropping the priced RBA hike.

items.future_rule: After closing AUDCAD, stay flat until a new Australia-versus-Canada policy, growth, inflation, or carry gap appears that is not merely the opposite of the trade just exited.
items.lesson: Do not reverse a closed AUDCAD fade on a same-session diplomacy or oil tape. An oil hold that re-supports CAD is an invalidation of the long, not a reason to own it.
items.sizing_assessment: A smaller 10m long reduced capacity risk versus the prior short but did not fix being the wrong side of oil-supported CAD.
items.thesis_assessment: The AU-over-CA long assumed CAD energy premium would skim. That catalyst did not dominate, so direction was wrong even though the cross isolation was still the right expression family.
items.timing_assessment: The long was held about six and a half days, long enough for the oil invalidation to matter. Unlike the prior short, this was not a two-day horizon squeeze; it was a bad reverse.
items.what_failed: The long converted an unfinished fade into a diplomacy and oil catalyst trade whose own oil invalidation then defined the loss.
items.what_worked: Closing on 29 Sep when oil was still supporting CAD respected the long's own oil invalidation rather than adding into the same reverse.

causal.assumptions_right: The CA-JP carry gap was real and paid. CADJPY isolated CA versus JP better than USD legs. BoJ did not hike during the hold. Flattening after the ToT pillar broke, rather than riding carry into 28 Oct, matched the original reason for the trade.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Durability of oil as CAD fundamental support; speed of ToT failure versus still-positive carry; hawkish-hold BoJ communication as a JPY-positive offset; two-way BoC event risk once the commodity premise was gone; treating post-exit drift to 112.23 as information to re-engage.
causal.causal_divergence: P&L was earned while oil and carry still agreed with CA-over-JP. After the slide, the economic driver of the CAD leg decoupled from still-positive carry and still-firm spot. Price continued to work after the reason died; that is residual momentum, not confirmation of the original belief.
causal.future_implication: Cross-CAD risk requires a live ToT or policy gap that survives a from-flat test. Closed-trade P&L and a few extra CADJPY pips are not that gap. AUDCAD stays off-limits as a reverse. EURJPY needs EA evidence that is not in this tape, so the book stays empty.
causal.observed_reality: Oil slid and knocked out the CAD ToT pillar; the long was closed 26 Oct at 112.04 from 110.9 for +154437; spot is now 112.23; BoC is polled at 2.50 on 28 Oct; BoJ is expected to hold with a hawkish lean; CORRA 2.24 vs TONA 1.227 still funds the cross; WTI 101.76 and Brent 115.81 are the current oil marks, with the slide magnitude itself unknown.
causal.original_belief: Oil-supported Canadian terms of trade plus a funded CORRA-over-TONA carry would keep CAD bid against JPY while BoJ remained the easier G10 central bank, so long CADJPY was the clean non-USD expression of that gap.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With oil as a hard invalidation, the desk would have flattened on the slide, still banked the harvest, and still refused both a 112.23 CADJPY re-entry and an AUDCAD reverse. Given only the present tape—ToT pillar already called broken, BoC tomorrow, BoJ hawkish-hold—CADJPY would not be opened from flat.

items.expression_assessment: CADJPY was the correct isolation of CA versus JP. Failure was not the pair choice and not a reason to migrate into AUDCAD or USD legs. The broken input was the CAD oil/ToT assumption inside an otherwise clean cross.

facts.invalidation: The CADJPY long is wrong if Brent no longer supports cheap CAD versus JPY, if the cheapness is a yen-haven bid rather than CAD lag, or if a non-recycled AU-versus-CA gap becomes the clearer cross.

items.future_rule: Into a BoC decision week, CADJPY and AUDCAD may be opened only as from-flat initiations with a live oil/ToT or policy differential; never as re-entry or reverse of a just-closed CADJPY long, and never on leftover pips after the pillar has already failed.
items.lesson: After a CADJPY ToT-carry long is closed because oil impaired the CAD pillar, do not reopen CADJPY and do not reverse AUDCAD unless that exact cross would be initiated from a flat book on new, independent AU-CA or CA-JP evidence.
items.sizing_assessment: Realized +154437 on a now-flat book. Notional, risk limit, and vol-scaled size are unknown (null) in this tape, so sizing can only be judged as non-catastrophic: the winner was harvested without leaving residual CADJPY into BoC.
items.thesis_assessment: The CA-over-JP relative-value thesis was right for the holding window while oil supported CAD and BoJ stayed easy. It became stale the moment the terms-of-trade pillar broke: carry alone was never the original reason to own CAD versus JPY into a home-bank meeting.
items.timing_assessment: Entry on 2 Oct at 110.9 caught the funded move. Exit on 26 Oct at 112.04, one session before the 28 Oct BoC, was the right date once ToT support was gone. The subsequent print at 112.23 is leftover drift, not evidence the exit was early in decision-quality terms.
items.what_failed: Oil/ToT was treated as a durable CAD pillar rather than a condition that can fail faster than policy. There was no pre-committed oil invalidation that forced an exit at the slide rather than after the pillar was already judged broken. Post-exit spot at 112.23 shows residual momentum after the reason died; that drift is a process trap, not a missed mandate to reopen into BoC week.
items.what_worked: CADJPY isolated a funded CA-over-JP view (CORRA above TONA, oil-supported CAD terms of trade, BoJ still the easier central bank) without Fed beta. The 2 Oct entry at 110.9 was paid through 26 Oct at 112.04 for +154437. Holding the cross rather than a USDCAD/USDJPY box kept the P&L on the intended differential while oil and carry aligned.
